summary: No national digital transformation strategy is on file; the civil service ministry began preparing a sectoral plan of its own in [August 2026](2026-08-04-libya-civil-service-ministry-national-digital-transformation-plan).
developments:
The Ministry of Civil Service held a preparation meeting on 4 August 2026 for a national digital transformation plan, with no timetable, budget, lead agency or published document behind it ([preparation meeting](2026-08-04-libya-civil-service-ministry-national-digital-transformation-plan)).

The National Digital Transformation Strategy is named elsewhere in this base as the parent of the country's digital identity work, but no text, period or costing for it is held.

summary: The National Telecommunications and Informatics Strategy 2023-2027 remains in force, with root servers delivered under it in [October 2025](2025-10-26 Libya launches root servers in Tripoli and Benghazi — digital sovereignty).
developments:
The strategy period runs to 2027 and nothing on file records a mid-term review, a successor or a costing.

Its one recorded delivery is the pair of root-server instances that entered service in Tripoli and Benghazi in October 2025, presented by the authority as a step in national control of internet infrastructure ([root servers](2025-10-26 Libya launches root servers in Tripoli and Benghazi — digital sovereignty)).

summary: The [2025-2030 digital agenda](2025-10-09-gia-national-agenda-digital-development-2025-2030) sets a broadband rollout to 2027 and records the laws behind it as unenacted.
developments:
The [agenda](2025-10-09-gia-national-agenda-digital-development-2025-2030) issued in October 2025 is the first standing digital development plan the base holds for Libya, and it puts broadband rollout on a horizon to 2027 while stating that the data protection and electronic commerce laws it relies on remain unenacted.

What is moving underneath it is wholesale access rather than a plan: the regulator and the fixed operator [set fibre-pair lease prices and opened access networks to private investment](2025-12-30-gaci-hatif-libya-fibre-pair-pricing-fttx-access-networks) in December 2025.

summary: A National Cloud Computing Policy went to national consultation with [ESCWA](2026-01-01-gia-national-cloud-computing-policy-escwa) in January 2026; the final text is not published.
developments:
The consultation was held on 1 January 2026 and the policy is framed as the arrangement for hosting government data and services, pressed on the state's sovereignty over its own data ([consultation](2026-01-01-gia-national-cloud-computing-policy-escwa)).

No draft text, timetable or hosting standard has been published since, so the base holds the intention and not the instrument.

summary: A [roadmap proposes an interoperability framework](2025-12-01-escwa-gia-lygif-interoperability-frameworks-roadmap) and none had been adopted as at December 2025.
developments:
The regional commission's [roadmap](2025-12-01-escwa-gia-lygif-interoperability-frameworks-roadmap) sets out best practice and proposes a Libyan government interoperability framework; nothing had been adopted when it was published.

The governance layer that exists is a method rather than a standard: the information authority's [national guide for government data](2022-12-01-gia-national-guide-for-government-data) sets a six-stage approach with no interface specification or schema behind it. The mandate to interconnect state bodies has sat with the authority since [a 2018 decision](2018-02-01-presidential-council-decision-130-2018-national-number-competences).

summary: The prime minister adopted a 2026-2030 [National Artificial Intelligence Strategy](2026-06-01-lana-dbeibah-adopts-ai-ethics-charter-national-strategy) on 1 June 2026, replacing the 2025-2030 edition published eight months earlier.
developments:
The first edition, prepared with ESCWA, was published in October 2025 ([2025-2030 edition](2025-10-30-national-ai-strategy-2025-2030-published-libyaherald)).

The 2026-2030 edition was adopted at an official ceremony alongside an ethics charter ([adoption](2026-06-01-lana-dbeibah-adopts-ai-ethics-charter-national-strategy)). Its targets are stated rather than measured: 80 per cent of government entities using artificial intelligence, 70 per cent activation of the national digital identity, 10,000 staff trained, 100 startups, half of government transactions automated and 70 per cent of paper records digitised ([adoption](2026-06-01-lana-dbeibah-adopts-ai-ethics-charter-national-strategy)).

summary: [Circular 18 of 2025](2025-07-01-cbl-circular-18-2025-banking-data-protection-regulation) bars all cross-border transfer of Libyan banking data and requires certified in-country hosting.
developments:
The central bank's [regulation](2025-07-01-cbl-circular-18-2025-banking-data-protection-regulation) is the strictest localisation rule the base holds for Libya: banking data may not leave the country, hosting must be certified to international information-security and card-industry standards, and [breaches carry a penalty of LYD 100,000 each](2025-07-02-cbl-circular-18-2025-data-protection-regime-banking-sector).

It is sectoral. No economy-wide localisation instrument exists, and the [national digital agenda](2025-10-09-gia-national-agenda-digital-development-2025-2030) records the general data protection law as still unenacted.

summary: The identity authority's Government Data Governance Policies moved from [presentation](2026-02-16 Libya's GIA presents Government Data Governance vision at cloud-computing workshop) in February 2026 to [first application](2026-04-23-gia-zakat-fund-data-governance-national-guide) in April, with no adoption instrument stated.
developments:
The policies were presented at a Tripoli cloud-computing workshop in February 2026 as a national vision for data ownership, integration and cybersecurity-by-design ([presentation](2026-02-16 Libya's GIA presents Government Data Governance vision at cloud-computing workshop)).

They were applied in April 2026 as the reference framework for the Libyan Zakat Fund's digital platforms, the only application on file ([application](2026-04-23-gia-zakat-fund-data-governance-national-guide)). The authority's own account is the sole source, and no adoption instrument or gazette date is stated, so the standing of the policies cannot be established from this base.

summary: A draft national open-data policy was issued in November 2025 alongside the [open government data platform](2025-11-27-gia-open-government-data-platform-launch); no adopted text has followed.
developments:
The identity authority launched the platform on 27 November 2025 with a draft national open-data policy and a National Technical Guide covering standards and metadata for adoption by government entities ([launch](2025-11-27-gia-open-government-data-platform-launch)).

Nine months on, the base holds no adopted policy, no adopting decision and no list of the entities that have taken the guide up ([workshop account](2026-02-16 Libya's GIA presents Government Data Governance vision at cloud-computing workshop)).

summary: No data-protection statute is in force; the [National Artificial Intelligence Strategy](2025-10-30-national-ai-strategy-2025-2030-published-libyaherald) sets 2026 as the target for one, with nothing enacted by August.
developments:
The strategy published in October 2025 names a data-protection law among its 2026 deliverables ([strategy](2025-10-30-national-ai-strategy-2025-2030-published-libyaherald)). Nothing had been enacted as at 10 August 2026, and the base holds no draft text, no sponsoring ministry and no parliamentary stage for it.

Personal-data systems have meanwhile continued to be built and launched without one.

summary: A comprehensive cybersecurity law is in drafting on the eastern legislative track, discussed with the [National Security Council](2026-07-16-parliament-national-security-cybersecurity-law-alwasat) in July 2026.
developments:
The House of Representatives established a committee for the draft under the Speaker's decision 115 of 2025, and drafting was discussed with the National Security Council on 16 July 2026 ([drafting](2026-07-16-parliament-national-security-cybersecurity-law-alwasat)).

No text has been published, no reading has been recorded, and the base holds nothing on how a law passed on that track would apply in the west of the country.

summary: [Law 8 of 2014](2014-03-24-qanun-8-lisanat-2014-bishan-alraqm-alwatani) creates the twelve-digit national number, mandatory from birth for every state service.
developments:
The [law](2014-03-24-qanun-8-lisanat-2014-bishan-alraqm-alwatani) is the statutory basis for everything built since: a twelve-digit number assigned from birth and required to obtain any state service.

The institution beneath it is older — the [civil registry authority created by decree in 1998](1998-08-01-qarar-115-lisanat-1998-inshaa-maslahat-alahwal-almadaniyya) — and the competences were redistributed by a [2018 presidential council decision](2018-02-01-presidential-council-decision-130-2018-national-number-competences) that gave the information authority the national database. No amending statute has been passed.

summary: A prime-ministerial decree of [6 March 2026](2026-03-06-cbl-mandates-epayments-state-revenue-fx-cut-libyaherald) obliges treasuries and collecting agencies to accept electronic payment, the first such instrument on file.
developments:
The decree was issued on 6 March 2026 and is reported alongside a cut in the foreign-exchange levy, making electronic acceptance a duty of state collecting bodies rather than an option ([decree](2026-03-06-cbl-mandates-epayments-state-revenue-fx-cut-libyaherald)).

The base holds no implementing regulation, no compliance deadline and no penalty for a body that does not comply.

summary: A [2018 decision](2018-02-01-presidential-council-decision-130-2018-national-number-competences) hands the information authority the national database and the mandate to interconnect state bodies.
developments:
The [decision](2018-02-01-presidential-council-decision-130-2018-national-number-competences) is the operative instrument: it redistributes the national number project's competences and gives the authority both the database and the linkage mandate.

The service it produced is running — [electronic linkage connecting national bodies to the central database](2023-02-07-gia-alrabt-aliliktruni), with no civil registry link named — while the framework that would standardise it is [still only proposed](2025-12-01-escwa-gia-lygif-interoperability-frameworks-roadmap).

summary: The [adopted AI strategy](2026-06-01-libya-national-ai-strategy-2026-2030) names the legislative vacuum and sets a four-stage law roadmap to 2030.
developments:
The [strategy adopted in June 2026](2026-06-01-libya-national-ai-strategy-2026-2030) is unusually direct about its own starting point: it names a legislative vacuum and sets a four-stage roadmap to legislation by 2030. No artificial intelligence statute is in force.

The instrument that arrived first is soft: the regulator [reopened the draft national artificial intelligence charter for public comment in April 2026, five weeks before adoption](2026-04-28-gaci-ai-ethics-charter-public-consultation-workshop), and the information authority [convened a meeting in April to move the strategy from drafting to implementation](2026-05-03-gia-meeting-launch-executive-initiatives-national-ai-strategy).

summary: [Law 6 of 2022](2022-10-04-libya-law-6-of-2022-electronic-transactions) covers electronic signatures, contracts and fifteen disclosures to online buyers; no e-commerce act follows it.
developments:
The [law](2022-10-04-libya-law-6-of-2022-electronic-transactions) enacted in October 2022 is the operative instrument for electronic dealing: signature and contract rules, and fifteen matters a seller must disclose to an online buyer.

It is not a full electronic commerce regime, and the [national digital agenda](2025-10-09-gia-national-agenda-digital-development-2025-2030) of October 2025 records the electronic commerce law as still unenacted alongside the data protection law.

summary: [Law 16 of 1963](1963-09-19-libya-law-16-of-1963-statistics-and-censuses) still governs statistics and censuses, its penalty scale unchanged since enactment.
developments:
The [statute](1963-09-19-libya-law-16-of-1963-statistics-and-censuses) creates the central statistics committee and remains the governing law, with penalties still expressed in the currency unit of 1963.

Nothing has replaced it. The [statistics development strategy that ran to 2023](2018-04-01-libyan-national-statistics-development-strategy-2018-2023) carried no adoption decree the base could locate and has not been renewed, so the sector runs on a sixty-three-year-old law and an expired plan.

summary: The [cabinet's draft bill](2022-10-08-libya-draft-law-national-information-system) sets a request-and-appeal procedure and remains unenacted.
developments:
The [draft law on the national information system](2022-10-08-libya-draft-law-national-information-system) would give Libya a request-and-appeal route to public records. It has not been enacted.

What publication happens is voluntary: the [audit bureau published its 2024 annual report on 31 December 2025 after delay](2025-12-31-libyan-audit-bureau-annual-report-2024-published), with no right-to-information law compelling it. The [constitutional declaration](2014-08-07-libya-constitutional-declaration-2011-consolidated) guarantees expression and privacy and creates no access right.

summary: No supervisory authority exists and none is named in the [strategy](2025-10-30-national-ai-strategy-2025-2030-published-libyaherald) that targets a data-protection law, leaving new platforms to protect data on instruction alone.
developments:
The National Artificial Intelligence Strategy sets a data-protection law for 2026 but does not name a regulator to administer it ([strategy](2025-10-30-national-ai-strategy-2025-2030-published-libyaherald)).

The practical consequence shows in the Libya Experts Forum registration platform, reported ready for launch in July 2026: those preparing it were instructed to protect registrants' data, with no statute and no regulator to apply ([platform](2026-07-23-libya-al-abed-preparations-libya-experts-forum)).

progress: Regressed, two new population-scale databases authorised with no protective framework behind them
summary: Two databases holding personal records were authorised in August 2026, one of [expatriate workers](2026-08-03-libya-interior-labour-ministries-unified-national-database-expatriate-labour) and one of [event participants](2026-08-09-libya-digital-exhibitions-platform-launch), neither with a stated legal basis.
developments:
The interior and labour ministries agreed a unified national database of expatriate workers on 3 August 2026, with a dedicated platform and no authorising instrument, retention limit or oversight body named ([database](2026-08-03-libya-interior-labour-ministries-unified-national-database-expatriate-labour)).

The economy and trade ministry launched an exhibitions and conferences platform on 9 August 2026 building an integrated record of organisers, participants and visitors, with no supplier, hosting arrangement or data-protection basis stated ([platform](2026-08-09-libya-digital-exhibitions-platform-launch)).

summary: Libya took the chair of the [Arab working group on artificial intelligence and digital infrastructure](2026-08-01-egypt-chairs-58th-aticm-executive-bureau-arab-ai-groups), declared for the [ITU Council](2026-07-26-libya-communications-informatics-delegation-regional-cooperation) and signed an [audit roadmap with Tunisia](2026-08-15-libya-tunisia-audit-ai-digital-roadmap).
developments:
The Arab ministers' executive bureau recorded Libya's allocation of the chair of the working group on artificial intelligence, data and digital infrastructure on 1 August 2026 ([allocation](2026-08-01-egypt-chairs-58th-aticm-executive-bureau-arab-ai-groups)).

A delegation canvassed the country's ITU Council candidacy bilaterally at the African Telecommunications Union plenipotentiary in Abuja in July 2026 ([candidacy](2026-07-26-libya-communications-informatics-delegation-regional-cooperation)).

Libya's Audit Bureau and Tunisia's Court of Auditors signed a phased roadmap in Amman on 15 August 2026 covering exchange of expertise, capacity building, digital systems and cooperation on artificial intelligence and its governance; no phase dates, budget or workplan is published ([roadmap](2026-08-15-libya-tunisia-audit-ai-digital-roadmap)).

summary: Libya [signed the United Nations cybercrime convention in October 2025](2025-10-26-libya-signs-un-cybercrime-convention-alwasat); neither it nor the 2010 Arab convention is ratified.
developments:
The Arab League's own tally records Libya as having [signed the 2010 convention on information technology offences and never ratified it](2017-02-20-arab-convention-it-offences-signature-ratification-list).

The pattern repeated: Libya [signed the United Nations Convention against Cybercrime at Hanoi in October 2025 among sixty states](2025-10-26-libya-signs-un-cybercrime-convention-alwasat), with the anti-corruption authority's head leading the delegation. Where harmonisation does bite it is technical rather than legislative: the standards bodies of Libya and Tunisia [concluded the twentieth meeting of their mutual recognition working group](2025-12-18-lncsm-libya-tunisia-mutual-recognition-task-force-20th-meeting) in December 2025.

summary: The [Medusa submarine cable](2025-05-12-medusa-submarine-cable-inaugurated-misrata-libyaherald) reaches Libya through Misrata as part of an eight-country Mediterranean system; no further landing has been recorded.
developments:
Medusa was inaugurated at Misrata in May 2025 as an 8,700 km system serving Italy, Spain, Portugal, Morocco, Tunisia, Greece, Egypt and Cyprus, with Tripoli and Benghazi landings planned ([inauguration](2025-05-12-medusa-submarine-cable-inaugurated-misrata-libyaherald)).

Nothing has been published since on either planned landing, so the country's share of a regional system remains a single station.

summary: [Circular 18 of 2025](2025-07-01-cbl-circular-18-2025-banking-data-protection-regulation) bans all cross-border transfer of Libyan banking data outright.
developments:
The central bank's [regulation](2025-07-01-cbl-circular-18-2025-banking-data-protection-regulation) prohibits banking data leaving Libya and requires hosting inside the country certified to international security and card-industry standards, with [a penalty of LYD 100,000 per breach](2025-07-02-cbl-circular-18-2025-data-protection-regime-banking-sector).

A flat prohibition is a harder rule than most transfer regimes: there is no adequacy route, no consent route and no derogation on the record. Outside banking, no general instrument governs transfers at all, the data protection law being [still unenacted](2025-10-09-gia-national-agenda-digital-development-2025-2030).

summary: No framework is adopted: a [roadmap proposes one](2025-12-01-escwa-gia-lygif-interoperability-frameworks-roadmap) and the [national data guide](2022-12-01-gia-national-guide-for-government-data) sets a method, not a standard.
developments:
The [national guide for government data](2022-12-01-gia-national-guide-for-government-data) of December 2022 sets a six-stage governance method and stops short of any interface specification or schema, which is what an interoperability standard would have to supply.

The [regional commission roadmap of December 2025](2025-12-01-escwa-gia-lygif-interoperability-frameworks-roadmap) proposes a framework and records none as adopted. Meanwhile the exchange layer runs without one, through the authority's [electronic linkage service](2023-02-07-gia-alrabt-aliliktruni) and the national data exchange already on the ledger.

summary: The standards body [adopted its 2026 plan, new specifications and a quality mark rule](2026-02-03-lncsm-supreme-committee-adopts-2026-plan-and-standards) in February 2026.
developments:
The governing statute is [Law 5 of 1990](1990-05-15-libya-law-5-of-1990-standards-and-metrology), which creates the standards centre and makes its standards binding nationwide, with a penalty ceiling frozen at LYD 1,000 since enactment.

The centre's supreme committee [reviewed the 2025 annual report and adopted a 2026 plan, new specifications and a quality mark licensing rule](2026-02-03-lncsm-supreme-committee-adopts-2026-plan-and-standards) in February 2026. No count of information technology standards adopted is published.

summary: Operators were convened in [April 2026](2026-04-22-gaci-ipv6-transition-libyaherald) to begin the move from IPv4 to IPv6, with no timetable or target published.
developments:
The communications authority convened operators on 22 April 2026 to start the transition ([convening](2026-04-22-gaci-ipv6-transition-libyaherald)).

No timetable, adoption target or measurement of current IPv6 traffic accompanies it, and the base holds no other national programme to take up an international technical standard.

summary: A [Libya Experts Forum](2026-07-23-libya-al-abed-preparations-libya-experts-forum) registration platform was reported ready for launch in July 2026, the one channel on file for outside expertise.
developments:
The application was reported ready for launch on 23 July 2026, intended to register experts willing to contribute to national work ([platform](2026-07-23-libya-al-abed-preparations-libya-experts-forum)).

No launch, registration count or terms of reference have been published since, and the base holds no other structured route for non-governmental contribution to policy.

summary: The [constitutional declaration](2014-08-07-libya-constitutional-declaration-2011-consolidated) guarantees expression and sets no consultation duty; two consultations ran anyway in 2026.
developments:
The [consolidated declaration](2014-08-07-libya-constitutional-declaration-2011-consolidated) guarantees expression and privacy and imposes no obligation to consult before adopting policy, so every consultation in Libya is discretionary.

Two ran in the window. The regulator [reopened the draft national artificial intelligence charter for public comment five weeks before adoption](2026-04-28-gaci-ai-ethics-charter-public-consultation-workshop) in April 2026, and the information authority and the development programme [opened community consultations for the seventh national human development report](2026-02-19-gia-undp-seventh-nhdr-community-consultations-launch) in February.

summary: [Zero development spend on the communications authority for January-February 2026](2026-02-28-cbl-revenue-expenditure-statement-jan-feb-2026), after LYD 41.2m in all of 2025.
developments:
The central bank's [2025 statement](2025-12-31-cbl-revenue-expenditure-statement-jan-dec-2025) puts the communications authority's spend at LYD 41.2m against total state outlay of LYD 136.8bn — about 0.03 per cent.

The [statement for January and February 2026](2026-02-28-cbl-revenue-expenditure-statement-jan-feb-2026) shows no development spend on the authority at all, with salaries also short. The fiscal frame did change: the governor [announced the first unified state budget in more than thirteen years](2026-04-11-cbl-governor-first-unified-budget-in-13-years) in April 2026, ending dual fiscal streams.

summary: Talks with the [People's Bank of China](2026-08-16-chinese-yuan-africa-cips-payment-network) point to a financing relationship, including yuan-denominated panda bonds for reconstruction; no agreement is held.
developments:
A newspaper account of August 2026 reports that talks between the Central Bank of Libya and the People's Bank of China cover both accession to China's payment network and an intention to issue yuan-denominated panda bonds to help fund post-conflict reconstruction ([account](2026-08-16-chinese-yuan-africa-cips-payment-network)).

No signed agreement, issue size or timetable is stated, and no central-bank statement is held, so the relationship rests on a single report.

summary: A [sixty-article partnership regulation](2025-07-23-libya-cabinet-decision-507-2025-ppp-contracts-regulation) was adopted in July 2025 and a [state seed fund](2025-01-23-qarar-23-lisanat-2025-sunduq-intilaqa-sharikat-al-ibtikar-al-nashia) created in January.
developments:
The [partnership regulation](2025-07-23-libya-cabinet-decision-507-2025-ppp-contracts-regulation) is the framework private capital would enter public projects through: sixty articles, with the courts holding jurisdiction over disputes and no digital-sector figure attached.

The [seed fund created in January 2025](2025-01-23-qarar-23-lisanat-2025-sunduq-intilaqa-sharikat-al-ibtikar-al-nashia) supports and guarantees financing for startup innovation companies and requires an artificial-intelligence-screened application platform, which is state money rather than private. Donor money is separate again: a [EUR 11.2m technical assistance project for public financial governance and digital investment runs 2026-2029](2026-05-06-expertise-france-invest4libya-project).

summary: Development partners carry the two named programmes on file, a [UNDP data-systems memorandum](2025-07-02 UNDP and Libya's GIA sign MoU on data systems and human development) and a [UNDP-backed institute](2025-11-01-planning-ministry-ai-cybersecurity-institute-alwasat), with no value published for either.
developments:
UNDP and the identity authority signed a memorandum on data systems and human development in July 2025 ([memorandum](2025-07-02 UNDP and Libya's GIA sign MoU on data systems and human development)), under which the Seventh National Human Development Report was in preparation as at February 2026 ([progress](2026-02-16 Libya's GIA presents Government Data Governance vision at cloud-computing workshop)).

The Ministry of Planning launched a professional master's institute in artificial intelligence and cybersecurity with UNDP in November 2025 ([institute](2025-11-01-planning-ministry-ai-cybersecurity-institute-alwasat)). Neither engagement carries a published value, duration or disbursement schedule, so the base can record partner activity but not partner financing.

summary: Commercial [5G](2026-01-29-almadar-launches-first-5g-tripoli-libyaherald) began in central Tripoli in January 2026 and the state operator is in [talks with Nokia](2026-07-16-libya-nokia-5g-cooperation-alwasat); no penetration figure is published.
developments:
Almadar Aljadid began the country's first commercial 5G service in central Tripoli on 29 January 2026, with extension to the rest of the country stated to follow ([launch](2026-01-29-almadar-launches-first-5g-tripoli-libyaherald)). A regional review a year later placed Libya among the North African markets where 5G is live ([review](2026-08-03-ookla-5g-north-africa-one-year-on)).

LTT met Nokia on 15 July 2026 on 5G cooperation, with no agreement announced ([meeting](2026-07-16-libya-nokia-5g-cooperation-alwasat)). No subscriber count, coverage share or penetration measure is published in this base, so what is recorded here is network availability rather than take-up.

summary: [74 per cent of women use the internet and household internet stands at 92 per cent](2025-10-01-mics7-libya-2024-2025-survey-findings-report) on the 2024-25 survey.
developments:
The regulator's own dashboard puts [9.06m internet users and 15.4m mobile lines for 2024](2024-01-01-gaci-penetration-and-usage-indicators-2024), a line count well above the population.

The household survey is the better instrument and gives a different picture: [92 per cent of women using mobile phones, 74 per cent using the internet, household internet at 92 per cent](2025-10-01-mics7-libya-2024-2025-survey-findings-report). The international agency series [carries 88 per cent internet use for 2022 and leaves every household and gender indicator unreported](2024-01-01-itu-digital-development-dashboard-libya).

summary: Operator tariffs run [from 0.5 LYD for 50MB to 80 LYD for 80GB](2026-09-03-almadar-aljadid-mobile-internet-packages-tariff); no regulated price basket is published.
developments:
The base holds no regulated tariff order and no affordability basket for Libya. What it holds is the retail cards: an [operator's live tariffs from 0.5 LYD for 50MB over a day to 80 LYD for 80GB over thirty days](2026-09-03-almadar-aljadid-mobile-internet-packages-tariff).

A competing [unlimited daily plan caps heavy use at 10 dinars through the operator's app](2026-01-25-ltt-yawmi-plus-unlimited-daily-internet-package). Neither is set against income, and no regulator series measures the basket as a share of earnings.

progress: Regressed, restored to eleven of twelve sites after a flood cut, most of them on satellite backup
summary: A flood severed the [Ghat to Tahala fibre link](2026-05-30-ghat-tahala-fibre-cut-restored-alwasat) on 27 May 2026; 11 of 12 sites were back within days, most on VSAT backup.
developments:
The link was cut by flooding on 27 May 2026 and restored to 11 of the 12 sites it serves, 91.7 per cent, with most running on VSAT backup rather than on fibre ([restoration](2026-05-30-ghat-tahala-fibre-cut-restored-alwasat)).

The base holds no route map, no capacity figure and no statement of when full fibre service returned, so the condition of the backbone after the cut cannot be established beyond the count of sites.

summary: The [Medusa cable](2025-05-12-medusa-submarine-cable-inaugurated-misrata-libyaherald) has been live at Misrata since May 2025 and no capacity or bandwidth figure has been published for it since.
developments:
The cable was inaugurated at Misrata in May 2025 ([inauguration](2025-05-12-medusa-submarine-cable-inaugurated-misrata-libyaherald)).

No capacity figure, utilisation share or price effect has been published in the fifteen months since, and the base holds no measure of international bandwidth per user for the country at all.

summary: Libya's [only registered exchange point shows zero peers connected](2024-04-25-peeringdb-tripoli-ixp-record).
developments:
The [registry record](2024-04-25-peeringdb-tripoli-ixp-record) for the Tripoli exchange lists no connected peers, so nothing measurable is exchanged there and domestic traffic between Libyan networks has no published local path.

Nothing in the base since records a peering agreement, a member count or a traffic figure for it.

summary: The state operator signed a capacity partnership with [Arabsat](2026-08-07-arabsat-and-ltt-sign-strategic-partnership-to-strengthen-libyas-digital-infrastructure) in August 2026 for the 30.5 degrees east position; no commercial terms are stated.
developments:
LTT and Arabsat announced a partnership on 7 August 2026 for capacity on Arabsat-6A at 30.5 degrees east ([partnership](2026-08-07-arabsat-and-ltt-sign-strategic-partnership-to-strengthen-libyas-digital-infrastructure)).

No value, duration, service date or retail offer is published, and the base holds nothing on licensing terms for any other satellite provider, including the low-orbit operators active elsewhere in the region.

summary: The only data-centre capacity on file is [Almadar Aljadid's](2025-10-26 Libya launches root servers in Tripoli and Benghazi — digital sovereignty) Tripoli and Benghazi facilities; a [2019 Tripoli project](2019-10-15-dcd-trans-saharan-tatweer-libyan-data-center) has nothing on file since.
developments:
Root-server instances entered service in October 2025 in Almadar Aljadid data centres in Tripoli and Benghazi, which is the base's only evidence that a national provider operates data-centre space ([root servers](2025-10-26 Libya launches root servers in Tripoli and Benghazi — digital sovereignty)).

A Trans-Sahara and Tatweer data centre was announced for Tripoli in October 2019 for delivery in early 2020, and nothing on it has appeared since ([announcement](2019-10-15-dcd-trans-saharan-tatweer-libyan-data-center)). No floor area, rack count, tier rating or customer figure is held for any facility in the country.

summary: A [tier III design certification](2026-09-03-uptime-institute-km4-data-center-litc-tripoli) is recorded for the national telecom company's KM-4 site, with no capacity disclosed.
developments:
The [certification record](2026-09-03-uptime-institute-km4-data-center-litc-tripoli) is the first independent assessment of a Libyan facility the base holds. It certifies design rather than construction or operation, and discloses no capacity figures.

The regulatory frame is behind it: the regulator [floated a first data centre and cloud licensing framework in February 2026, at which point storage firms were operating unpermitted](2026-02-15-gaci-workshop-data-centre-cloud-regulatory-framework). A ministry [opened its own data centre in April 2026](2026-04-15-wazir-al-talim-yaftatih-markaz-al-bayanat-wal-minassat-al-raqmiyya).

summary: The [national backup policy](2020-01-23-nissa-data-backup-policy) mandates geographic separation of copies; no Libyan disaster recovery site was located.
developments:
The information security authority's [policy](2020-01-23-nissa-data-backup-policy) requires backup copies to be geographically separated, which is the rule. No named Libyan site satisfying it appears anywhere in the base.

The one recorded test of resilience went the other way and came out well: the central bank [told the parliamentary finance committee in July 2026 that banking systems were fully restored after a cyberattack with no accounts hit](2026-07-05-cbl-governor-hor-finance-committee-systems-restored).

summary: Policy requires [99.9 per cent power uptime, dual water sources and 24 hours of fuel](2020-01-23-nissa-physical-security-policy-data-centres) at data centres, against a grid that [lost 1,350 MW in one failure](2026-07-18-libya-national-blackout-1350-mw-lost-alwasat).
developments:
The [physical security policy](2020-01-23-nissa-physical-security-policy-data-centres) sets the standard: 99.9 per cent power uptime, dual water sources, twenty-four hours of fuel and staffed network operations.

The grid it is written against [lost 1,350 MW in July 2026, darkening most of the country after a tripped 400kV line](2026-07-18-libya-national-blackout-1350-mw-lost-alwasat). No Libyan facility publishes its own power or water provision against the policy, so compliance cannot be established from the record.

progress: Mixed, capacity added against a national failure inside the window
summary: [8.2 GW of capacity in 2023](2024-12-03-eia-country-analysis-brief-libya-electricity), a [1,350 MW national failure in July 2026](2026-07-18-libya-national-blackout-1350-mw-lost-alwasat), a new plant firing in August.
developments:
Capacity reached [a record 8.2 GW in 2023 after years of blackouts](2024-12-03-eia-country-analysis-brief-libya-electricity).

Reliability did not follow. A [failure in July 2026 lost 1,350 MW and darkened most of the country](2026-07-18-libya-national-blackout-1350-mw-lost-alwasat), blamed by the ministry on a tripped 400kV line. In August the utility [fired the first of four units at a new South Tripoli plant toward 1,320 MW of added capacity](2026-08-28-gecol-south-tripoli-station-unit-one-first-fire).

summary: [400 off-grid solar systems at 310 kW peak](2026-09-03-reaol-remote-areas-solar-electrification-project) for remote clusters and border posts.
developments:
The renewable energy authority's [programme](2026-09-03-reaol-remote-areas-solar-electrification-project) is the only off-grid electrification the base holds: 400 systems, 310 kW peak, for remote population clusters and border posts.

On the grid side, work [began in January 2026 for a Cyrenaica settlement cut off since 1999](2026-01-04-libya-omar-al-mukhtar-settlement-electrified-after-1999). Neither source gives a count of households reached.

summary: The central bank's card system collapsed in [May 2026](2026-05-27-cbl-epayment-system-crash-2m-pos-libyaherald) under two million transactions in a day, against a terminal estate of 170,149.
developments:
The electronic payment system failed on 27 May 2026 when 2m transactions were attempted across 67,000 acceptance points in a single day ([failure](2026-05-27-cbl-epayment-system-crash-2m-pos-libyaherald)).

The estate had grown from 150,205 terminals in 2024 to 170,149 by February 2026 ([estate](2026-03-03-cbl-record-epayment-qr-launch-alwasat), [2025 volumes](2026-02-21-cbl-epayment-2025-stats-313bn-alwasat)).

Nothing has been published on the cause, on remediation or on capacity headroom since, and the base holds no equivalent measure for any other government system.

summary: The one capacity fact on file is a foreign vendor, [Huawei](2026-07-26-libya-lana-khidma-madaniya-huawei-tahawwul-raqmi), scoping civil-service systems under a compliance undertaking to the regulator.
developments:
The telecommunications regulator suspended Huawei's activities nationwide on 17 August 2025 ([suspension](2025-08-17-lana-gti-suspends-huawei-activities-libya)) and reinstated the company three days later on a compliance undertaking ([reinstatement](2025-08-20-lana-gti-huawei-libya-agreement)).

By July 2026 the company was scoping digital transformation work on civil-service systems ([scoping](2026-07-26-libya-lana-khidma-madaniya-huawei-tahawwul-raqmi)). The base holds nothing on in-house capability: no civil-service technical headcount, no maintenance arrangement, and no statement of which systems the state can run without a vendor.

progress: Mixed, a central bank breach and a caseload unpublished since early 2025 against a new interior ministry cooperation agreement
summary: The [central bank was breached](2026-06-24-cbl-cyber-incident-alwasat) in June 2026 with data later published on a dark-web site, while the interior ministry signed a [cooperation agreement](2026-08-12-libya-interior-ministry-cybersecurity-cooperation) in August.
developments:
The Central Bank of Libya isolated systems in June 2026 and a sample of bank data was later published on a dark-web site ([incident](2026-06-24-cbl-cyber-incident-alwasat), [context](2026-08-04-isdb-training-central-bank-of-libya-sukuk-ai-risk-management)).

The interior ministry and the national telecommunications company signed a technical cooperation agreement reported on 12 August 2026 covering cybersecurity, shared platforms and equipment at ministry sites, with no value, duration or delivery date published ([agreement](2026-08-12-libya-interior-ministry-cybersecurity-cooperation)).

The last cybercrime caseload published is 135 cases and 188 devices seized in the first quarter of 2025 ([caseload](2025-03-30-interior-cybercrime-cases-q1-2025-alwasat)). No national readiness assessment, incident-response body or breach-notification duty is held.

summary: [LY-NDEX](2026-07-09-gia-ly-ndex-ly-dnid-aml-information-exchange-workshop) was positioned in July 2026 as the state's data-exchange spine for inter-agency verification, with no connected-entity or transaction figure published.
developments:
The general information authority and the commercial register office are examining the interconnection of their systems ([report](2026-08-27-nabd-)). It is an examination; no design, standard or date is stated.

The identity authority presented LY-NDEX at an interior ministry workshop concluding on 8 July 2026 as pillar infrastructure for information exchange between agencies, including anti-money-laundering and counter-terrorist-financing compliance ([workshop](2026-07-09-gia-ly-ndex-ly-dnid-aml-information-exchange-workshop)).

No legal basis, connected-entity count, service catalogue or transaction volume has been published, so the base can record the claim made for the exchange but not its operation.

summary: [LY-DNID](2026-07-09-gia-ly-ndex-ly-dnid-aml-information-exchange-workshop) is presented together with the national data exchange as the verification layer for anti-money-laundering checks across agencies.
developments:
At the July 2026 workshop the identity authority set the national digital identity beside LY-NDEX as the pair on which inter-agency verification and compliance checks are to run ([workshop](2026-07-09-gia-ly-ndex-ly-dnid-aml-information-exchange-workshop)).

The only sector named as a consumer of it is financial compliance. No ministry, service or agency is listed as connected, and no count of identity verifications performed for another system is published.

summary: The [diabetes authority's system links insulin dispensing to the national number](2026-05-03-alhaya-alwataniya-limarad-alsukari-almanzuma-alilktruniya-almuwahhada), the first named clinical link to the identity layer.
developments:
The health information centre [runs the national health data platform and hosts health data on a mobile operator's cloud](2022-01-01-moh-libya-markaz-almalumat-waltawthiq-alsihi), which is the standing arrangement.

Two links were added in the window. The ministry [activated an electronic system tracking medicines from pharmacy intake to hospital dispensing](2025-10-06-wizarat-alsihha-manzuma-iliktruniya-litatabu-harakat-aladwiya) in October 2025, and the diabetes authority [launched a unified system in May 2026 tying insulin dispensing to the national number](2026-05-03-alhaya-alwataniya-limarad-alsukari-almanzuma-alilktruniya-almuwahhada).

summary: The education data system [now carries private schools](2026-07-22-lana-idraj-muassasat-altaalim-alkhass-manzumat-bayanat-altaalim) and [links schools by network](2026-01-01-moe-dic-almasharie-nizam-bayanat-altaalim), with no link to the civil registry.
developments:
The system [launched for the 2023/24 year](2023-09-01-moe-dic-itlaq-manzumat-bayanat-altaalim) covering school-level staff and institutions, and [logged 498,653 pupils across 4,981 schools for 2025/26 with entry still under way](2025-10-20-moe-dic-ihsaiyyat-alaam-aldirasi-2025-2026).

In July 2026 the ministry [finished loading private-school data and launched a parent verification platform](2026-07-22-lana-idraj-muassasat-altaalim-alkhass-manzumat-bayanat-altaalim). Its own account of the data centre [describes school links by wide-area network and mapping, with no connection to the civil registry or the national number](2026-01-01-moe-dic-almasharie-nizam-bayanat-altaalim) — so the system is complete internally and isolated externally.

summary: The [Libyan Zakat Fund's](2026-04-23-gia-zakat-fund-data-governance-national-guide) digital platforms took integration through the national data exchange as their reference model in April 2026, the only such case on file.
developments:
The identity authority's April 2026 guide records the Zakat Fund adopting integration via LY-NDEX, digital identity verification and the once-only principle for its platforms ([guide](2026-04-23-gia-zakat-fund-data-governance-national-guide)).

No other social-protection body is recorded as connected, no data-sharing agreement is published, and the fund's own integration is described as a reference case rather than as completed work.

summary: Enforcement in 2026 [revoked 225 national identification numbers and passports](2026-01-02-attorney-general-civil-registry-id-fraud-crackdown-libyaherald) and suspended 61 family records, with a trade in forged numbers [still reported](2026-04-19-fake-national-numbers-for-sale-alwasat).
developments:
The attorney general's office suspended 61 family records and revoked 225 national identification numbers and passports in January 2026 ([enforcement](2026-01-02-attorney-general-civil-registry-id-fraud-crackdown-libyaherald)); ten further numbers were cancelled at Al-Marj the same month ([cancellations](2026-01-14-almarj-civil-registry-fake-national-numbers-alwasat)).

A trade in forged national numbers was still being reported in April 2026 ([trade](2026-04-19-fake-national-numbers-for-sale-alwasat)), and parliament had warned of breaches in the civil registry system in December 2025 ([warning](2025-12-08 Libyan Parliament warns of breaches in Civil Registry national ID system)). No count of fraudulent numbers in circulation and no remediation programme is published.

An independent analysis built on 66 official publications of the Attorney General's office to April 2026 found 278,969 nationality files exposed to forgery over a 43-year window, with 10,620 families and more than 4,000 individuals implicated, and named five mechanisms including direct manipulation of the registry database ([analysis](2026-08-26-alwasat-libya-civil-registry-nationality-fraud)).

summary: Holders of administrative rather than national numbers remain outside services gated on the national number, with [no published resolution](2025-06-07-administrative-numbers-holders-anger-alwasat).
developments:
Protests were reported in June 2025 by holders of administrative numbers excluded from services that require a national identification number ([protests](2025-06-07-administrative-numbers-holders-anger-alwasat)).

No resolution has been published since, and the base holds no registration coverage figure: no count of the population holding a national number, and no count of those in the administrative category.

summary: The [civil registry match completed across 257 offices covering 97 per cent of households](2024-09-03-intilaqa-mutabaqat-bayanat-257-maktab-ahwal-madaniyya); the project is still unfinished.
developments:
The registry authority [created by decree in 1998](1998-08-01-qarar-115-lisanat-1998-inshaa-maslahat-alahwal-almadaniyya) is the source layer for every Libyan credential, and the [electronic-to-paper match completed across 257 offices covering 97 per cent of households](2024-09-03-intilaqa-mutabaqat-bayanat-257-maktab-ahwal-madaniyya).

The government [reviewed the unfinished project and its links to other agencies in July 2026 without giving a completion date](2026-07-09-lana-bin-ghalbun-tatwir-manzumat-alsijil-almadani-intilaqa). The passport authority separately [set out an electronic passport project and printer renewal](2025-09-02-lana-maslahat-aljawazat-tatwir-manzumat-isdar-aljawazat) to a prime-ministerial committee in September 2025.

summary: The [Level 3 biometric tier](2026-04-19-gia-cbl-level-3-biometric-digital-identity-ekyc) of the national digital identity entered technical trials with the central bank and several banks in April 2026.
developments:
The identity authority and the Central Bank of Libya put the biometric tier into technical trials with several banks in April 2026, ahead of its use in banking know-your-customer checks ([trials](2026-04-19-gia-cbl-level-3-biometric-digital-identity-ekyc)).

The system is named the Digital Identity Management System for Citizens in that release and LY-DNID in the July one, and no enrolment count, authentication volume or assurance standard is published for either name ([July release](2026-07-09-gia-ly-ndex-ly-dnid-aml-information-exchange-workshop)).

summary: [Law 8 of 2014](2014-03-24-qanun-8-lisanat-2014-bishan-alraqm-alwatani) makes the national number mandatory from birth; no birth-to-number workflow is described.
developments:
The [statute](2014-03-24-qanun-8-lisanat-2014-bishan-alraqm-alwatani) is unambiguous that the twelve-digit number attaches from birth and is required for every state service, so the entitlement exists in law.

What the base does not hold is any account of how a birth becomes a number in practice. The [registry match across 257 offices](2024-09-03-intilaqa-mutabaqat-bayanat-257-maktab-ahwal-madaniyya) was a reconciliation of existing records, and the [project remained unfinished in July 2026](2026-07-09-lana-bin-ghalbun-tatwir-manzumat-alsijil-almadani-intilaqa).

summary: The [civil registry database is still under development](2026-03-01-lana-alnaib-alaam-qaidat-bayanat-alsijil-almadani-aliliktruniyya) and the [linkage service names no civil registry connection](2023-02-07-gia-alrabt-aliliktruni).
developments:
The information authority's [electronic linkage service](2023-02-07-gia-alrabt-aliliktruni) connects national bodies to the central database and names no civil registry link among them.

The registry's own electronic database is still being built: the attorney general [reviewed progress on it in March 2026 amid a forgery investigation](2026-03-01-lana-alnaib-alaam-qaidat-bayanat-alsijil-almadani-aliliktruniyya), and the government [reviewed the wider project again in July](2026-07-09-lana-bin-ghalbun-tatwir-manzumat-alsijil-almadani-intilaqa) without a completion date.

summary: The [National ID Number](2024-09-06 Libya's Project Intilaqa matches Civil Registry electronic data with paper records) gates SIM registration, passports, bank accounts, marriage and voting, and that position has not moved since 2024.
developments:
The number is in force and required across those services, which makes it the country's operative credential rather than one of several ([gating](2024-09-06 Libya's Project Intilaqa matches Civil Registry electronic data with paper records)).

Nothing has been published since 2024 on how many transactions are gated on it, on which further systems have taken it up, or on what a resident without one can still obtain.

summary: The central bank directed banks to activate [QR acceptance](2026-03-03-cbl-record-epayment-qr-launch-alwasat), permitted [e-wallets for resident foreigners](2026-03-11-cbl-allows-foreigners-ewallets-circular-alwasat) and launched a [stand-in processing service](2026-06-17-cbl-epaix-2026-softpos-visa-standin-libyaherald) in 2026.
developments:
Banks were directed to activate QR-code acceptance by 8 March 2026 ([directive](2026-03-03-cbl-record-epayment-qr-launch-alwasat)).

Circular 9 of 2026, issued on 11 March, permitted resident foreigners to hold e-wallets on passport and residency with daily transfer caps ([circular](2026-03-11-cbl-allows-foreigners-ewallets-circular-alwasat)).

A national stand-in processing service was launched at the EPAIX conference on 17 June 2026 to keep card payments working through communications and banking disruption ([service](2026-06-17-cbl-epaix-2026-softpos-visa-standin-libyaherald)). The bank sets the rules, the deadlines and the shared infrastructure, and no other body is recorded acting on the payment market.

summary: [Ratibak Lahzi](2026-07-30-libya-central-bank-76-percent-public-sector-ratibak-lahzi) carried July 2026 salaries for 1.7m of 2.2m public employees, 76 per cent, up from 72 per cent in March.
developments:
The real-time salary system launched in August 2025 with about 2m records collected, the eastern government refusing to share employee banking data ([launch](2025-08-11 Libya's CBL launches 'Ratebk Lahzi' real-time salary system)).

Enrolment reached 72 per cent in March 2026 ([March](2026-04-02-cbl-ratibak-lahzi-march-salaries-1-585m-72-percent)), 75 per cent in June ([June](2026-06-25-cbl-ratibak-lahzi-june-salaries-75-percent)) and 76 per cent in July, when July salaries were executed through it ([July](2026-07-30-libya-central-bank-76-percent-public-sector-ratibak-lahzi), [confirmation](2026-07-30-cbl-ratibak-lahzi-july-salaries-76-percent)).

About 500,000 public employees remain outside it, with no published breakdown of who they are ([remainder](2026-07-30-libya-central-bank-76-percent-public-sector-ratibak-lahzi)).

summary: State treasuries and collecting agencies must accept electronic payment from [March 2026](2026-03-06-cbl-mandates-epayments-state-revenue-fx-cut-libyaherald), the first duty of its kind placed on revenue bodies.
developments:
The obligation reaches treasuries and collecting agencies and was issued together with a cut in the foreign-exchange levy ([mandate](2026-03-06-cbl-mandates-epayments-state-revenue-fx-cut-libyaherald)).

No collection figure, adoption rate or list of complying agencies has been published since, so the base holds the requirement and no measure of what it has changed.

summary: The Prime Minister [ordered treasuries to accept electronic payment of all state revenues](2026-03-05-lgcc-qarar-60-lisanat-2026-jibayat-aliradat-alamma-iliktruniyyan) in March 2026.
developments:
The [decision](2026-03-05-lgcc-qarar-60-lisanat-2026-jibayat-aliradat-alamma-iliktruniyyan) activates electronic collection of all public revenues and dues at Libyan treasuries, which is the mandate side.

The delivery side is smaller and specific: the central bank [exempted point-of-sale fees for tax, customs and port payments and deployed 130 terminals as a first phase](2026-05-10-libyaherald-cbl-ending-cash-collection-taxes-customs-pos), moving toward ending cash collection. The bank's own [payment and settlement page](2022-08-04-cbl-payment-and-settlement) sets out the rails behind it and gives no business or government transaction figures.

summary: [Instant transfers](2026-02-21-cbl-epayment-2025-stats-313bn-alwasat) ran 18.3m times in 2025, and acceptance widened to [petrol stations](2026-01-15-jumhuria-first-petrol-station-epayment-libyaherald) and to [phones used as terminals](2026-06-17-cbl-epaix-2026-softpos-visa-standin-libyaherald).
developments:
LYPAY ONEPAY carried 18.3m transfers worth LD 108.7bn in 2025, the first published volumes for the service ([volumes](2026-02-21-cbl-epayment-2025-stats-313bn-alwasat)).

Jumhouria Bank brought card acceptance to petrol stations on 15 January 2026, the first such service ([petrol stations](2026-01-15-jumhuria-first-petrol-station-epayment-libyaherald)).

SoftPOS was launched at EPAIX on 17 June 2026, letting NFC phones act as card terminals ([launch](2026-06-17-cbl-epaix-2026-softpos-visa-standin-libyaherald), [conference](2026-06-16-cbl-epaix-softpos-visa-alwasat)). No count of active wallets, or of merchants accepting by either route, is published.

summary: Banking apps reached [4.30m subscribers](2026-03-03-cbl-record-epayment-qr-launch-alwasat) by February 2026 and electronic payment value reached [LD 643bn](2026-08-05-central-bank-of-libya-to-increase-cash-liquidity-at-branches) in the first seven months of 2026.
developments:
Electronic payment value ran at LD 136bn in 2024, LD 389bn in 2025 and LD 643bn between 1 January and 31 July 2026 ([2026 to date](2026-08-05-central-bank-of-libya-to-increase-cash-liquidity-at-branches), [2025](2026-01-20-cbl-epayment-2025-up-186pc-389bn-libyaherald)).

Banking-app subscribers stood at 4.30m in February 2026, and 200.7m transactions worth LD 313.6bn were recorded in 2025 ([subscribers](2026-03-03-cbl-record-epayment-qr-launch-alwasat), [2025 total](2026-02-21-cbl-epayment-2025-stats-313bn-alwasat)).

Part of that movement is scarcity rather than choice: branch cash withdrawals were capped at LD 3,000 a customer, and LD 4,000 in the south, from 9 August 2026 ([cash limits](2026-08-05-central-bank-of-libya-to-increase-cash-liquidity-at-branches)).

summary: [Foreign-currency Visa acceptance](2026-06-17-cbl-epaix-2026-softpos-visa-standin-libyaherald) went live on local terminals in June 2026, and banks are reported set to join [China's CIPS network](2026-08-16-chinese-yuan-africa-cips-payment-network).
developments:
Visa acceptance in foreign currency was launched on local points of sale at EPAIX on 17 June 2026, giving cards issued abroad a route into the domestic network ([launch](2026-06-17-cbl-epaix-2026-softpos-visa-standin-libyaherald)).

A newspaper account of 16 August 2026 reports Libyan banks set to join China's Cross-Border Interbank Payment System after talks between the two central banks; no accession date, participant list or signed agreement is stated, and no central-bank statement is held ([account](2026-08-16-chinese-yuan-africa-cips-payment-network)).

summary: Card-payment surcharges were prohibited and made enforceable by a [Municipal Guard notice](2026-08-03-libya-municipal-guard-warns-against-debit-card-surcharge) in August 2026, after spreads of up to 20 per cent.
developments:
The Municipal Guard issued an enforcement notice on 2 August 2026 against merchants adding a surcharge to card payments, with spreads of up to 20 per cent reported before it ([notice](2026-08-03-libya-municipal-guard-warns-against-debit-card-surcharge)).

No penalty schedule, complaint route or enforcement count has been published, and the base holds no other consumer-protection measure covering electronic payment.

summary: The interior and labour ministries agreed a [unified national database of expatriate workers](2026-08-03-libya-interior-labour-ministries-unified-national-database-expatriate-labour) in August 2026, with a dedicated platform and no authorising instrument.
developments:
The two ministries agreed the database on 3 August 2026 and named a dedicated platform for it ([agreement](2026-08-03-libya-interior-labour-ministries-unified-national-database-expatriate-labour)).

No build or timetable is published, and the base holds no register of the citizen population against which to set it, so the only population-register movement on file covers non-citizens.

summary: [Project Intilaqa](2024-09-06 Libya's Project Intilaqa matches Civil Registry electronic data with paper records) matched the civil registry's electronic and paper records across 257 offices to 97 per cent, and no later figure has been published.
developments:
The project matched electronic data to paper records in 257 offices and printed 1.8m family records, reaching 97 per cent completion as at September 2024 ([matching](2024-09-06 Libya's Project Intilaqa matches Civil Registry electronic data with paper records)). It had been outstanding since the mid-1970s.

Nothing has been published in the two years since on the remainder, on error rates found, or on how the matched register is now maintained.

summary: [National postal addressing](2025-01-01 Libya launches national postal addressing project (Tripoli, Hay Al-Andalus)) is in phase one covering 42,000 buildings in one Tripoli district, with no completion figure published since.
developments:
Phase one covers 42,000 buildings in Hay Al-Andalus, Tripoli, and was under way at the start of 2025 ([phase one](2025-01-01 Libya launches national postal addressing project (Tripoli, Hay Al-Andalus))).

No later count, no extension to other districts and no link to any other register has been published, so the address layer that other systems would draw on does not yet exist beyond one district.

summary: A [Unified Economic Number](2026-07-18-libya-unified-economic-number) was authorised in July 2026, the [chambers of commerce system](2026-03-02-unified-chambers-of-commerce-digital-system-libyaherald) went live in March, and the [one-stop shop](2026-02-20 Libya to reactivate One-Stop Shop for company registration (Commercial Registry Authority)) is again promised.
developments:
Decision No. 348 of 2026 authorised implementation of a Unified Economic Number with a national council constituted for it, and no timetable, budget or legal basis for the data linkage is stated ([decision](2026-07-18-libya-unified-economic-number)).

The Unified Digital System for Chambers of Commerce went live on 1 March 2026 with digital certificates of origin, chamber registration and a verification channel for customs ([system](2026-03-02-unified-chambers-of-commerce-digital-system-libyaherald)).

Reactivation of the One-Stop Shop for company registration under Law No. 23 of 2010 was agreed in February 2026, against a record of repeated past failures to reform registration and nothing yet delivered ([reactivation](2026-02-20 Libya to reactivate One-Stop Shop for company registration (Commercial Registry Authority))).

The health ministry's registration portal has registered 131 local and 53 foreign pharmaceutical companies and is being extended to the products themselves, confining attendance at the ministry to the final stage and licence collection ([portal](2026-08-26-libyaherald-pharmagate-digital-registration)) - a sectoral register rather than the general one.

summary: A [Unified Social Registry](2025-06-23 Libya's PM Dabaiba approves Unified Social Registry project) draft was approved by the prime minister in June 2025 and nothing on its build has been published since.
developments:
The draft was approved on 23 June 2025 ([approval](2025-06-23 Libya's PM Dabaiba approves Unified Social Registry project)).

No build, budget, timetable, lead agency or data source has been published in the fourteen months since, and no count of households or beneficiaries held in any existing social-protection list is available in this base.

summary: [Biometric voter verification](2024-08-19 Libya implements biometric voter verification in municipal council elections) was piloted in four municipalities at the 2024 municipal elections and no extension has been published.
developments:
The commission used biometric verification in four municipalities at the municipal council elections of August 2024 ([pilot](2024-08-19 Libya implements biometric voter verification in municipal council elections)).

No evaluation, no extension to national elections and no register size have been published since, so the register's coverage and its link to the national identification number cannot be established from this base.

summary: The tax administration was [entirely paper-based with no register system](2024-08-01-imf-libya-ta-report-redesign-of-income-tax-forms) in August 2024; a unified tax system has since gone live.
developments:
The fund's [technical assistance report](2024-08-01-imf-libya-ta-report-redesign-of-income-tax-forms) of August 2024 is blunt: Libya's tax administration ran entirely on paper with no register system behind it.

The unified tax system carried on the ledger since December 2025 is the answer to that finding, and the [electronic revenue collection mandate of March 2026](2026-03-05-lgcc-qarar-60-lisanat-2026-jibayat-aliradat-alamma-iliktruniyyan) extends the same logic to collection. No taxpayer count has been published against either.

summary: [Benghazi resumed limited registry transactions in April 2026](2026-04-26-almarsad-altasjil-alaqari-banghazi-almuamalat-alidariyya), against a suspension standing since 2011.
developments:
The registration authority has [issued certificates only, with substantive registration suspended since 2011](2019-02-19-aladel-altasjil-alaqari-bayna-alwaqi-walmamul), and [cadastral mapping covers two-thirds of the country on a fragmented spatial data infrastructure](2023-01-01-unhabitat-land-administration-land-rights-libya).

In [April 2026 the Benghazi office resumed limited administrative transactions including mortgage and ownership transfer](2026-04-26-almarsad-altasjil-alaqari-banghazi-almuamalat-alidariyya) despite the suspension. Municipalities are building their own holdings alongside: [a mayor reviewed registry records for a state-property inventory](2026-04-21-lana-tajoura-alsijil-alaqari-hasr-mumtalakat-aldawla) that month.

summary: A [Sustainable Medical Supply Platform](2026-08-17-libya-mso-digital-supply-platform) entered pilot in August 2026 to manage pharmaceutical procurement, inventory and distribution for the state importer.
developments:
The pilot phase began on 17 August 2026, built with and run by NSR International for Information Technology, a subsidiary of the Libyan Foreign Investment Company, for the state importer of the country's medicines, and aimed at a unified national medical-supply database ([pilot](2026-08-17-libya-mso-digital-supply-platform)).

No cost, pilot scope, timetable or facility count is stated, and the base holds no other health information system for the country.

summary: [498,653 pupils across 4,981 schools](2025-10-20-moe-dic-ihsaiyyat-alaam-aldirasi-2025-2026) logged for 2025/26, with private schools loaded in July 2026.
developments:
The system [launched for 2023/24](2023-09-01-moe-dic-itlaq-manzumat-bayanat-altaalim) and now carries [498,653 pupils across 4,981 schools for 2025/26, with entry still under way](2025-10-20-moe-dic-ihsaiyyat-alaam-aldirasi-2025-2026).

Coverage widened in July 2026 when the ministry [finished loading private-school institutions and launched a parent verification platform](2026-07-22-lana-idraj-muassasat-altaalim-alkhass-manzumat-bayanat-altaalim). A separate [smart geographic map of 102 technical education institutions](2026-02-04-gia-smart-geographic-map-technical-education-institutions) was launched in February 2026 as the sector's first system-wide digital record.

summary: The social insurance system [moved from modelling to procedural build-out](2026-03-04-ssf-alintiqal-ila-alamaliyyat-alijraiyya-almanzuma-aldamaniyya) in March 2026.
developments:
The diagnostic baseline is a 2022 assessment finding [social assistance delivery paper-based, with no unified registry and no identity check](2022-04-01-worldbank-wfp-social-assistance-programs-delivery-libya-codi).

The fund [moved its integrated insurance system from modelling into procedural build-out in March 2026](2026-03-04-ssf-alintiqal-ila-alamaliyyat-alijraiyya-almanzuma-aldamaniyya). The only published throughput figure is a transfer count: [1.22m families and 1.21m spouse cards](2026-05-18-lana-minhat-alzawja-walawlad-almasarif-altijariyya) for the second quarter of 2026, paid through commercial banks.

summary: The prosecution's digital case-file system [tallied 108,939 convictions in absentia](2025-11-11-lana-alnaib-alaam-majlis-huquq-alinsan-manzumat-altahawwul-alraqmi) over four years.
developments:
Digitisation started with the record layer: the prosecution service [digitised 400,000 evidence-gathering records across six appeal courts](2023-10-29-libyaobserver-alniyaba-alamma-raqmanat-mahadir-wathaiq-qadaiyya) in 2023.

By November 2025 the office was reporting from it, telling the United Nations human rights body that its [digital case-file system tallies 108,939 in-absentia convictions over four years](2025-11-11-lana-alnaib-alaam-majlis-huquq-alinsan-manzumat-altahawwul-alraqmi). No court-side case management system is named in the base.

summary: A [Unified Tax System](2025-12-14 Libya launches Unified Tax System and activates Tax Police) launched in December 2025, with a [Tax Police](2025-12-14 Libya launches Unified Tax System and activates Tax Police) role activated alongside it for oversight and compliance.
developments:
The system was launched on 12 December 2025 with further platforms stated for 2026, and the Tax Police role was activated with the interior ministry two days earlier ([launch](2025-12-14 Libya launches Unified Tax System and activates Tax Police)).

No registered-taxpayer count, filing volume, revenue effect or list of the further platforms has been published since, so the base records the launch and nothing about its operation.

summary: A [port trade service](2026-08-06-libya-electronic-cargo-monitoring-ports) began taking vessel arrivals and cargo manifests electronically at two ports in August 2026, with [chambers cooperation](2026-08-21-libya-herald-libyan-customs-authority-general-union-chambers) under discussion.
developments:
The Port Trade Service was activated at Tripoli and Al-Khoms on 5 August 2026, receiving vessel arrival notifications and cargo manifests electronically and presented as a control on undervalued or banned imports and on currency smuggling through fake trade ([activation](2026-08-06-libya-electronic-cargo-monitoring-ports)).

The customs authority and the general union of chambers of commerce discussed strengthening digital cooperation on 20 August 2026, with no memorandum or data-exchange arrangement on record ([discussions](2026-08-21-libya-herald-libyan-customs-authority-general-union-chambers)). No instrument establishing the service is held, no other port is covered, and no transaction figure is published.

summary: [Cadastral mapping covers two-thirds of the country](2023-01-01-unhabitat-land-administration-land-rights-libya) on a fragmented spatial data infrastructure.
developments:
The housing agency's analysis [puts cadastral coverage at two-thirds of Libya and finds the spatial data infrastructure fragmented](2023-01-01-unhabitat-land-administration-land-rights-libya), which is the base's only national assessment.

Nothing has consolidated it. The registration authority [issues certificates with substantive registration suspended since 2011](2019-02-19-aladel-altasjil-alaqari-bayna-alwaqi-walmamul), and the movement in the window is municipal: [a council building an integrated state-property database after a twenty-year planning freeze](2026-06-26-lana-aljufra-qaidat-bayanat-amlak-aldawla).

summary: Four state platforms moved in 2026: [e-visas](2026-08-20-libya-herald-libya-reports-2-325-e-visa), an [export window](2026-07-30-libya-herald-unified-export-window-leda), a [government reporting tool](2026-04-10-ly-govrep-government-reporting-platform-activated-libyaherald) and an [exhibitions register](2026-08-09-libya-digital-exhibitions-platform-launch), with usage published for two.
developments:
The electronic visa service took 2,325 applications from 103 nationalities between 1 July and 17 August 2026, of which 67.1 per cent were approved ([usage](2026-08-20-libya-herald-libya-reports-2-325-e-visa)).

The Electronic Unified Export Window processed LD 79.5m of exports from April to July 2026, with 354 companies registered and 190 products exported, two thirds of orders going to Tunisia ([export window](2026-07-30-libya-herald-unified-export-window-leda)).

LY-GOVREP was activated on 9 April 2026 as the unified performance-monitoring tool for public entities ([activation](2026-04-10-ly-govrep-government-reporting-platform-activated-libyaherald)), after preliminary operation with 60 cabinet entities ([preliminary](2025-07-20 Libya's GIA launches national government-reports platform LY-GOVREP)).

An exhibitions and conferences platform was launched on 9 August 2026 as the first specialised system for that sector ([launch](2026-08-09-libya-digital-exhibitions-platform-launch)).

summary: [BaladiyaBOT](2026-04-25-tripoli-baladiyabot-municipal-digital-assistant-libyaherald), a municipal digital assistant, went into development in April 2026 and is piloting in one Tripoli municipality.
developments:
Development began on 19 April 2026 and the assistant is piloting in Tripoli Centre municipality ([development](2026-04-25-tripoli-baladiyabot-municipal-digital-assistant-libyaherald)).

It is the only municipal digital service on file. No count of municipalities with connectivity, systems or equipment is published, and no national programme for local-government infrastructure is held in this base.

summary: A [municipal council leaders database](2026-03-27-lgm-qaidat-bayanat-shamila-lil-majalis-al-baladiyya) and a [council state-property database](2026-06-26-lana-aljufra-qaidat-bayanat-amlak-aldawla) were begun in 2026.
developments:
The ministry's own digitalisation began with correspondence: [internal mail moved to electronic form with paper phased out](2023-11-02-lgm-tahawwul-raqami-murasalat-iliktruniyya-baladiyat) in 2023.

Record-building followed. The ministry [started a comprehensive database of municipal council leaders in March 2026, still missing deputy data](2026-03-27-lgm-qaidat-bayanat-shamila-lil-majalis-al-baladiyya); a mayor [reviewed registry records for a state-property inventory in April](2026-04-21-lana-tajoura-alsijil-alaqari-hasr-mumtalakat-aldawla); and a council [moved to an integrated state-property database in June](2026-06-26-lana-aljufra-qaidat-bayanat-amlak-aldawla) after a twenty-year planning freeze.

summary: Influenza sentinel surveillance [expanded to 15 sites](2025-09-29-ncdc-warshat-al-tarassud-al-shamil-lil-influwanza-mawaqi-jadida) in September 2025.
developments:
Health data systems were rebuilt around the national platform [after the Derna floods](2024-01-01-who-emro-libya-annual-report-2023), which is the base's account of where the current architecture came from.

The reach beyond the cities is measured in surveillance posts rather than clinics: [15 sentinel sites with new posts at Misrata and Zliten](2025-09-29-ncdc-warshat-al-tarassud-al-shamil-lil-influwanza-mawaqi-jadida) from September 2025. No count of clinics running an electronic record is published.

summary: The ministry's data centre [links schools by wide-area network](2026-01-01-moe-dic-almasharie-nizam-bayanat-altaalim); no rural school detail is published.
developments:
The ministry's [own project account](2026-01-01-moe-dic-almasharie-nizam-bayanat-altaalim) describes schools linked by wide-area network and mapped geographically, without saying how many schools are connected or where they are.

The [data centre opened in April 2026](2026-04-15-wazir-al-talim-yaftatih-markaz-al-bayanat-wal-minassat-al-raqmiyya) alongside the ministry's platforms, again with no rural breakdown. The system carries [498,653 pupils across 4,981 schools](2025-10-20-moe-dic-ihsaiyyat-alaam-aldirasi-2025-2026), which counts records rather than connections.

summary: The electronic match [completed across 257 civil registry offices covering 97 per cent of households](2024-09-03-intilaqa-mutabaqat-bayanat-257-maktab-ahwal-madaniyya).
developments:
The [match](2024-09-03-intilaqa-mutabaqat-bayanat-257-maktab-ahwal-madaniyya) is the widest geographic digital exercise the base records for Libya: 257 offices, 97 per cent of households reconciled between paper and electronic records.

It is a reconciliation rather than a live system, and the [project remained unfinished when the government reviewed it in July 2026](2026-07-09-lana-bin-ghalbun-tatwir-manzumat-alsijil-almadani-intilaqa), with no completion date given.

summary: A [digital records system for police stations](2025-12-31-amn-tarabulus-tudashshin-manzumat-al-tahawwul-al-raqami) launched at the end of December 2025, in the capital.
developments:
The Tripoli security directorate [launched the system on 31 December 2025](2025-12-31-amn-tarabulus-tudashshin-manzumat-al-tahawwul-al-raqami), which is the first station-level digital record the base holds for Libya.

It is the capital's directorate. No deployment to stations elsewhere is recorded, and no station count is published.

summary: The one working case is a [municipal assistant](2026-04-25-tripoli-baladiyabot-municipal-digital-assistant-libyaherald) in pilot; the [strategy's targets](2026-06-01-lana-dbeibah-adopts-ai-ethics-charter-national-strategy) for administrative use are stated rather than measured.
developments:
BaladiyaBOT, in pilot in one Tripoli municipality since April 2026, is the only artificial-intelligence tool on file in day-to-day administrative use ([assistant](2026-04-25-tripoli-baladiyabot-municipal-digital-assistant-libyaherald)).

The National Artificial Intelligence Strategy adopted in June 2026 sets 80 per cent of government entities using artificial intelligence and half of government transactions automated as targets ([strategy](2026-06-01-lana-dbeibah-adopts-ai-ethics-charter-national-strategy)). Neither is measured, and no baseline for either is published.

summary: The [medical supply platform](2026-08-17-libya-mso-digital-supply-platform) in pilot is described as artificial-intelligence-enabled, with no statement of what the component does.
developments:
The platform entered pilot on 17 August 2026 as an artificial-intelligence-enabled national system for pharmaceutical procurement, inventory and distribution ([pilot](2026-08-17-libya-mso-digital-supply-platform)).

What the artificial-intelligence component does is not described, no model or supplier component is named, and no other sectoral information system in the country is recorded using one.

summary: [LIBIGPT](2025-10-28-libigpt-first-generative-ai-launched-libyaherald) launched in October 2025 as the country's first domestic generative artificial-intelligence system.
developments:
The system was launched on 28 October 2025 and is presented as the first generative artificial-intelligence system built in the country ([launch](2025-10-28-libigpt-first-generative-ai-launched-libyaherald)).

No user count, model description, training data statement or funding source has been published since, and no second domestic system has appeared in the base.

summary: The prime minister adopted an [AI Ethics Charter](2026-06-01-lana-dbeibah-adopts-ai-ethics-charter-national-strategy) on 1 June 2026 committing the state to human decision-making over automated systems in sensitive sectors.
developments:
The charter was adopted at an official ceremony alongside the artificial intelligence strategy and commits the state to justice, transparency and accountability, safeguards individuals' digital rights and centres human decision-making over automated systems in sensitive sectors ([charter](2026-06-01-lana-dbeibah-adopts-ai-ethics-charter-national-strategy)).

It is a reference for government, private and academic bodies rather than a binding instrument. No enforcement body, complaint route or sanction is named, and no statute on artificial intelligence is in force.

progress: Mixed, an identity-technology export against bank systems bought from foreign vendors
summary: A Libyan firm supplies [Niger's biometric passport system](2025-06-30 Libyan firm Al Itissan Al-Jadeed wins Niger biometric passport national ID contract), while banks build their digital services with [foreign vendors](2026-04-25-finnovate-libyan-banks-digital-expansion-alwasat) and a [national satellite](2026-08-04-libyan-authority-scientific-research-national-digital-transformation-platform) sits at design stage.
developments:
Al Itissan Al-Jadeed won Niger's biometric passport and national identity contract in June 2025, a rare identity-technology export, and no delivery milestone has been published since ([contract](2025-06-30 Libyan firm Al Itissan Al-Jadeed wins Niger biometric passport national ID contract)).

Tadamon Bank was reported building with JMR Infotech, and Seraj Islamic Bank with Network International, in April 2026, on vendor accounts ([build-outs](2026-04-25-finnovate-libyan-banks-digital-expansion-alwasat)).

The scientific research authority discussed a national earth-observation satellite at design stage in August 2026, with no budget, timetable or launch partner stated ([satellite](2026-08-04-libyan-authority-scientific-research-national-digital-transformation-platform)).

summary: A [national incubator in Tripoli](2026-01-01-al-hadina-al-tiknulujiyya-al-barnamaj-al-watani-lil-mashruat) and a [university incubator running a first competition](2026-07-30-ikhtitam-musabaqat-nawat-lil-mashruat-al-taqniyya-2026).
developments:
The small-enterprise programme runs a [technology incubator with Tripoli premises, training and a seed-grant admission route](2026-01-01-al-hadina-al-tiknulujiyya-al-barnamaj-al-watani-lil-mashruat).

Universities are the other host. One [crowned five ventures from more than 600 entries in its first technology competition](2026-07-30-ikhtitam-musabaqat-nawat-lil-mashruat-al-taqniyya-2026) in July 2026, and another [added licensed design and certification training for students and startups through two agreements](2026-02-13-jamiat-gharyan-solidworks-markaz-al-riyada-wal-ibtikar) in February.

summary: A [state seed fund](2025-01-23-qarar-23-lisanat-2025-sunduq-intilaqa-sharikat-al-ibtikar-al-nashia) was created in January 2025, requiring an AI-screened application platform.
developments:
The [decision](2025-01-23-qarar-23-lisanat-2025-sunduq-intilaqa-sharikat-al-ibtikar-al-nashia) creates a fund to support and guarantee financing for startup innovation companies, and requires applications to run through an artificial-intelligence-screened platform.
