Demand is visible where it has been counted: [more than 600 entries to a single university technology competition](2026-07-30-ikhtitam-musabaqat-nawat-lil-mashruat-al-taqniyya-2026) in 2026. No count of Libyan startups, investment total or survival rate is published.

summary: The only civil-service training on file is an [Islamic Development Bank executive programme](2026-08-03-islamic-development-bank-trains-central-bank-of-libya-officials-on-cybersecurity) for central bank officials, run once in July 2026.
developments:
The programme ran in Jeddah from 27 to 30 July 2026 for Central Bank of Libya officials on cybersecurity and artificial-intelligence risk management ([programme](2026-08-03-islamic-development-bank-trains-central-bank-of-libya-officials-on-cybersecurity), [account](2026-08-04-isdb-training-central-bank-of-libya-sukuk-ai-risk-management)).

Participant numbers, curriculum and any standard it works to are unstated, and no ministry-wide or government-wide digital skills programme is recorded in this base.

summary: A [skills assessment platform](2026-04-14-eu4skills-qudurat-digital-skills-assessment-platform) neared launch in April 2026 to measure digital skills against the labour market.
developments:
The [platform](2026-04-14-eu4skills-qudurat-digital-skills-assessment-platform), modelled on a French instrument, is the first attempt the base records to measure Libyan digital skills rather than assert them.

Delivery around it is programme-shaped: a [vendor innovation campus opened at the largest university in July 2026 with a 150-seat national artificial intelligence cohort](2026-07-21-jamiat-tarabulus-samsung-innovation-campus-libya), and a [technology foundation opened a sixth two-month bootcamp in cloud tooling, software development and cybersecurity](2026-07-13-al-muassasa-al-libiyya-lil-taqniya-barnamaj-al-tadrib-al-mihani-6). No population-level literacy measure exists yet.

summary: [About 4,500 pupils competed in a national informatics olympiad](2026-01-08-moe-al-ulimbiyad-al-libi-lil-malumatiyya-nihaiyyat) and a [licensing code puts 20 of 100 accreditation points on digital transformation](2026-06-17-moe-qarar-844-2026-aldalil-alshamil-lilmadaris-alkhassa).
developments:
The [olympiad](2026-01-08-moe-al-ulimbiyad-al-libi-lil-malumatiyya-nihaiyyat) concluded in January 2026 with about 4,500 pupils competing nationwide and 24 finalists, which is the widest counted school-level participation the base holds.

The structural moves are two: a [municipality reached a first agreement in April to bring coding and artificial intelligence teaching into its model schools](2026-04-09-tarabulus-al-markaz-idmaj-taalim-al-barmaja-al-madaris-al-namudhajiyya), and the [private-school licensing code adopted in June puts 20 of its 100 accreditation points on digital transformation](2026-06-17-moe-qarar-844-2026-aldalil-alshamil-lilmadaris-alkhassa). A [district office trained secondary staff in classroom artificial intelligence tools](2026-08-04-abu-salim-100-muallim-sibirani) in August.

summary: A professional master's [institute in artificial intelligence and cybersecurity](2025-11-01-planning-ministry-ai-cybersecurity-institute-alwasat) opened in November 2025, and a [higher-education research cloud](2026-08-04-libyan-authority-scientific-research-national-digital-transformation-platform) was approved in August 2026.
developments:
The Ministry of Planning launched the institute with UNDP on 1 November 2025, the only postgraduate qualification in these subjects on file ([institute](2025-11-01-planning-ministry-ai-cybersecurity-institute-alwasat)).

The scientific research authority's scientific committee approved a higher-education and research cloud platform on 4 August 2026, described by the authority as built on Microsoft 365 ([platform](2026-08-04-libyan-authority-scientific-research-national-digital-transformation-platform)). No enrolment, graduation or faculty figure is published for either, and no other university facility is recorded.

progress: No change, a first count with no earlier figure behind it
summary: The largest university's technology faculty reports [1,208 cumulative graduates, none in cybersecurity or data science and AI](2026-01-01-jamiat-tarabulus-kulliyat-taqniyat-al-malumat-haqaiq).
developments:
The faculty's [own facts page](2026-01-01-jamiat-tarabulus-kulliyat-taqniyat-al-malumat-haqaiq) gives 1,208 graduates cumulatively and records that none has yet come out of the cybersecurity or the data science and artificial intelligence tracks.

It is a supply figure with no destination attached: nothing in the base counts Libyan technology graduates entering employment. The training that is being added sits outside the degree pipeline, in [bootcamps](2026-07-13-al-muassasa-al-libiyya-lil-taqniya-barnamaj-al-tadrib-al-mihani-6) and a [150-seat vendor cohort](2026-07-21-jamiat-tarabulus-samsung-innovation-campus-libya).

summary: The one analytical contribution on file is the [Seventh National Human Development Report](2026-02-16 Libya's GIA presents Government Data Governance vision at cloud-computing workshop), in preparation under a UNDP memorandum with the identity authority.
developments:
UNDP and the identity authority signed a memorandum on data systems and human development in July 2025 ([memorandum](2025-07-02 UNDP and Libya's GIA sign MoU on data systems and human development)), and the report was in preparation as at February 2026 ([progress](2026-02-16 Libya's GIA presents Government Data Governance vision at cloud-computing workshop)).

No domestic think tank, university department or research centre is recorded contributing to digital policy, and the report itself has not been published.

summary: The [Raqib platform](2026-09-03-mansat-raqib-lil-shakawi-wal-balaghat) takes complaints and violation reports against about 750 state bodies.
developments:
The oversight authority [launched the platform at a Tripoli anti-corruption event in December 2025](2025-12-09-alwasat-aca-launches-raqib-corruption-reporting-platform).

It is live and its scope is stated: [complaints and violation reports against about 750 reportable state bodies](2026-09-03-mansat-raqib-lil-shakawi-wal-balaghat). No count of reports received or resolved is published, so its use cannot be measured from the record.

summary: A [consultative forum of about 120 members, 35 per cent women](2026-07-22-unsmil-structured-dialogue-platform-page), with no binding power.
developments:
The United Nations mission's [own account](2026-07-22-unsmil-structured-dialogue-platform-page) is candid about the limit: about 120 members, 35 per cent of them women, and no binding power over any decision.

Other participation is issue-specific and did move: [stakeholders neared consensus on a missing-persons draft law](2026-04-09-unsmil-undp-libyan-stakeholders-draft-law-missing-persons) at a March 2026 meeting, and the information authority [opened community consultations for the seventh national human development report](2026-02-19-gia-undp-seventh-nhdr-community-consultations-launch), including [a session dedicated to women](2026-07-02-gia-community-consultation-session-women-7th-national-human-development-report).

summary: An [eleven-point gender gap in account ownership](2025-06-01-cbl-national-financial-inclusion-strategy-2025-2029) against [74 per cent of women using the internet](2025-10-01-mics7-libya-2024-2025-survey-findings-report).
developments:
The central bank's [financial inclusion strategy](2025-06-01-cbl-national-financial-inclusion-strategy-2025-2029) puts the gender gap in account ownership at eleven points and access to mobile or internet banking at 14 per cent overall.

Connectivity is not what stands in the way: the household survey puts [92 per cent of women use mobile phones and 74 per cent use the internet](2025-10-01-mics7-libya-2024-2025-survey-findings-report). The international agency series [leaves every Libyan gender indicator unreported](2024-01-01-itu-digital-development-dashboard-libya), so the survey is the only sex-disaggregated evidence the base holds.

summary: The [digital accessibility policy moved from plan to mandatory compliance](2026-02-04-gia-launches-implementation-path-national-digital-accessibility-policy-escwa) in February 2026.
developments:
The statutory frame is old and analogue: [the 1987 disability law](1987-08-09-qanun-5-lisanat-1987-fi-shan-al-muaqin) imposes shelter, access and financial-aid duties and carries no digital-accessibility mandate.

The information authority [launched the implementation path of the national digital accessibility policy with regional commission support in February 2026](2026-02-04-gia-launches-implementation-path-national-digital-accessibility-policy-escwa), moving it from plan to compulsory compliance. Market provision is thin and specific: an operator [halved data pricing on a line restricted to certified deaf and hard-of-hearing users](2025-09-24-libyana-netwasel-line-sign-language-tariff).

summary: [Registered foreign residents were opened to electronic wallets](2026-03-11-cbl-allows-foreign-residents-e-wallets-daily-transfer-limits) in March 2026, on lower transfer limits.
developments:
Registration itself is the agency's rather than the state's: [44,223 refugees registered on the agency's own system with biometric enrolment deployed from August](2020-01-01-unhcr-libya-registration-and-profiling) 2020.

Financial access moved in the window. The central bank [opened electronic wallets to Libya's registered foreign residents with lower daily transfer categories](2026-03-11-cbl-allows-foreign-residents-e-wallets-daily-transfer-limits) in March 2026, and a [commercial bank launched the first such wallet, requiring no bank account](2026-03-16-bank-of-commerce-and-development-first-e-wallet-expat-residents-workers). Both reach the base through press reporting rather than a published circular.

summary: [Household internet at 92 per cent](2025-10-01-mics7-libya-2024-2025-survey-findings-report), with off-grid solar and university networks extending reach.
developments:
The household survey puts [household internet at 92 per cent and internet use among women at 74 per cent](2025-10-01-mics7-libya-2024-2025-survey-findings-report), which is high for the region and leaves the divide sitting elsewhere than access to a connection.

Where the state is closing gaps it is doing so through power and campus networks: [400 off-grid solar systems for remote clusters and border posts](2026-09-03-reaol-remote-areas-solar-electrification-project), [grid work for a settlement cut off since 1999](2026-01-04-libya-omar-al-mukhtar-settlement-electrified-after-1999), and a [university completing the second phase of its unified fibre network](2026-02-23-lana-wadi-al-shatii-university-unified-network-phase-two).

summary: The [2018-2023 strategy](2018-04-01-libyan-national-statistics-development-strategy-2018-2023) expired unrenewed, with no adoption decree ever located.
developments:
The [strategy](2018-04-01-libyan-national-statistics-development-strategy-2018-2023) was Libya's first, produced with international support, and the base could locate no decree adopting it.

Its term ended in 2023 and no successor has been published, leaving the statistical system running on [a 1963 statute](1963-09-19-libya-law-16-of-1963-statistics-and-censuses) and no current plan.

summary: A [2024-25 household survey](2025-10-01-mics7-libya-2024-2025-survey-findings-report) was published, and the authority [declared census readiness](2026-07-02-gia-confirms-technical-readiness-general-population-census-project) in July 2026.
developments:
The [multiple indicator cluster survey for 2024-25](2025-10-01-mics7-libya-2024-2025-survey-findings-report) is the most recent national household evidence the base holds, and supplies most of what is known about Libyan connectivity by sex and household.

The census is a different matter: the information authority [confirmed its technical readiness for the general population census and accompanying censuses in July 2026](2026-07-02-gia-confirms-technical-readiness-general-population-census-project), and the census itself remains unscheduled.

summary: [More than 8,000 procurement tenders were analysed](2026-01-04-gia-analysis-key-indicators-government-procurement-tenders-platform-2025) from platform data for 2025.
developments:
The information authority [completed an analysis of key indicators from the government procurement and tenders platform covering more than 8,000 tenders for 2025](2026-01-04-gia-analysis-key-indicators-government-procurement-tenders-platform-2025), which is administrative data used as statistics rather than merely held.

Sector capacity is being built to the same end: the agriculture ministry and the food agency [closed a two-week programme training 32 staff for the national agricultural statistics plan](2026-07-23-lana-wizarat-alziraa-alfao-alkhutta-alraisiyya-lilihsaat-alziraiyya) in July 2026.

summary: The [government open data platform](2025-11-27-gia-open-government-data-platform-launch) carries indicators over 91 datasets, joined in 2026 by an [information-for-all committee](2026-07-23-libya-technology-foundation-ifap-national-committee) and a [trial mineral map](2026-08-13-libya-digital-mineral-map-trial-launch).
developments:
The platform was launched on 27 November 2025 and by February 2026 carried indicators covering 91 datasets ([platform](2025-11-27-gia-open-government-data-platform-launch), [indicators](2026-02-16 Libya's GIA presents Government Data Governance vision at cloud-computing workshop)).

A National Committee for the Information for All Programme was established under Decision No. 50 of 2026 and met first on 20 July ([committee](2026-07-23-libya-technology-foundation-ifap-national-committee)).

A trial national digital mineral map was launched on 12 August 2026 on a database of roughly 1,200 ore and mineral indicators with geological maps at 1:250,000 scale, and no access terms, licence or publication date is stated ([mineral map](2026-08-13-libya-digital-mineral-map-trial-launch)).

summary: Officials were [trained on the geospatial platform and its AI tools](2026-05-12-fao-libya-strengthens-geospatial-platforms-ai-tools-water-oasis-management) in May 2026, with a second phase in coordination.
developments:
The platform [launched in March 2024](2024-03-30-launching-the-geospatial-platform-merwat-libya) by the agriculture and water ministries with international agency backing is the standing instrument.

Two things moved. Stakeholders [opened coordination on a second-phase irrigation decision-support platform](2026-02-09-libya-ministry-agriculture-merwat-2-national-stakeholders-coordination-meeting) in February 2026, and officials were [trained in May on the platform and artificial intelligence tools for water and oasis data](2026-05-12-fao-libya-strengthens-geospatial-platforms-ai-tools-water-oasis-management). Libya's [first drought strategy embeds vegetation-index and gravimetric satellite data in national planning](2026-01-26-undp-national-drought-management-strategy-and-action-plan-libya).

summary: Libya was [named a pilot for early-warning upgrades](2026-04-22-wmo-pooling-global-wisdom-address-global-climate-challenges) under a trilateral memorandum in April 2026.
developments:
The meteorological service [credited satellite imagery for its August 2024 flood warnings](2024-08-20-wmo-parts-of-libya-affected-by-extreme-weather-lnmc), which is the base's evidence that imagery reaches operational forecasting.

In [April 2026 the world meteorological body named Libya a pilot for early-warning upgrades under a trilateral memorandum with Chinese development and meteorological agencies](2026-04-22-wmo-pooling-global-wisdom-address-global-climate-challenges). The national earth-observation satellite the ledger carries remains a plan.

summary: United States engagement runs to a research cloud on [Microsoft 365](2026-08-04-libyan-authority-scientific-research-national-digital-transformation-platform) and an infrastructure memorandum between the state holding company and [KBR](2026-01-25-lptic-kbr-mou-5g-infrastructure-libyaherald).
developments:
LPTIC signed a memorandum with KBR on 25 January 2026 covering infrastructure and 5G, with no value or timetable published ([memorandum](2026-01-25-lptic-kbr-mou-5g-infrastructure-libyaherald)).

The scientific research authority approved a higher-education platform on 4 August 2026 that it describes as built on Microsoft 365, the only named dependence on a United States cloud provider in this base ([platform](2026-08-04-libyan-authority-scientific-research-national-digital-transformation-platform)). No hyperscaler has a data centre, region or commitment recorded in the country.

summary: Chinese engagement covers a [ZTE modernisation framework](2026-03-09-ltt-zte-mou-mwc-barcelona), [Huawei's return](2025-08-20-lana-gti-huawei-libya-agreement) after a three-day suspension, and reported accession to [China's payment network](2026-08-16-chinese-yuan-africa-cips-payment-network).
developments:
LTT signed a memorandum with ZTE at Mobile World Congress on 9 March 2026 covering 4G and 5G, e-wallet, e-commerce, content delivery and terminals, with no value or timetable ([memorandum](2026-03-09-ltt-zte-mou-mwc-barcelona)).

Huawei was suspended nationwide by the regulator on 17 August 2025 and reinstated three days later on a compliance undertaking ([reinstatement](2025-08-20-lana-gti-huawei-libya-agreement)).

Libyan banks are reported set to join China's Cross-Border Interbank Payment System, with yuan-denominated panda bonds also raised, on a single newspaper account ([account](2026-08-16-chinese-yuan-africa-cips-payment-network)).

summary: European engagement on file is one programme: [GIZ's municipal support](2026-04-25-tripoli-baladiyabot-municipal-digital-assistant-libyaherald), funded by the European Union and Germany, behind a municipal assistant in pilot.
developments:
BaladiyaBOT is being developed under the GIZ Support to Municipalities in Libya III programme, funded by the European Union and the German development ministry, and development began on 19 April 2026 ([programme](2026-04-25-tripoli-baladiyabot-municipal-digital-assistant-libyaherald)).

No value, duration or wider European digital engagement is recorded, and no European Union instrument covering the country's digital transformation is held in this base.

summary: Gulf engagement runs through two institutions: [Arabsat](2026-08-07-arabsat-and-ltt-sign-strategic-partnership-to-strengthen-libyas-digital-infrastructure) for satellite capacity and the [Islamic Development Bank](2026-08-04-isdb-training-central-bank-of-libya-sukuk-ai-risk-management) for central bank training.
developments:
LTT and Arabsat announced a capacity partnership on 7 August 2026, with no commercial terms published ([partnership](2026-08-07-arabsat-and-ltt-sign-strategic-partnership-to-strengthen-libyas-digital-infrastructure)).

The Islamic Development Bank ran an executive programme in Jeddah in late July 2026 for central bank officials on cybersecurity and artificial-intelligence risk ([programme](2026-08-04-isdb-training-central-bank-of-libya-sukuk-ai-risk-management)). No Gulf sovereign fund, hyperscaler or bilateral digital agreement is recorded, so the relationship is institutional rather than financial.

summary: Libya and India agreed cooperation on [artificial intelligence and quantum skills](2026-02-01-libya-india-ai-quantum-upskilling-libyaherald) in February 2026, with no programme document published.
developments:
The cooperation was agreed on 1 February 2026 and covers upskilling in artificial intelligence and quantum technologies ([cooperation](2026-02-01-libya-india-ai-quantum-upskilling-libyaherald)).

No programme document, participant numbers, funding or delivery date has been published since, and no other Indian engagement is recorded in the base.
